question:
A nuclear power station delivers an electrical output of $500\,\text{MW}$. The overall efficiency of conversion of fission energy to electrical energy is $\eta=0.30$.</br>
Assume each fission of $^{235}\!U$ releases $Q=200\,\text{MeV}$ of energy as heat.</br>
Take $1\,\text{MeV}=1.602\times10^{-13}\,\text{J}$, $N_A=6.022\times10^{23}\,\text{mol}^{-1}$, and $1\,u=1.66\times10^{-27}\,\text{kg}$.</br>

(a) Determine the thermal power that must be produced in the reactor core.</br>
(b) Find the fission rate (fissions per second).</br>
(c) Estimate the mass of $^{235}\!U$ consumed per day (assume one fission per nucleus).</br>
(d) Using mass–energy equivalence, estimate the mass actually converted to energy per day and evaluate the statement:</br>
“Although about kilograms of fuel undergo fission per day, only grams of mass are converted to energy; the rest remains as mass in fission products and released neutrons.”

options.A: $P_{th}\approx 1.67\times10^9\,\text{W}$, fission rate $\approx 5.20\times10^{19}\,\text{s}^{-1}$, fuel consumed $\approx 1.75\,\text{kg/day}$, mass converted $\approx 1.6\,\text{g/day}$, and the statement is correct
options.B: $P_{th}\approx 1.67\times10^8\,\text{W}$, fission rate $\approx 5.20\times10^{18}\,\text{s}^{-1}$, fuel consumed $\approx 0.175\,\text{kg/day}$, mass converted $\approx 16\,\text{g/day}$, and the statement is correct
